newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SUNFLOWER HARVEST THREATENED BY FUNGUS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SUNFLOWER HARVEST THREATENED BY FUNGUS.

text.p: Hungary's sunflower seed harvest is threatened by fungal diseases and weeds, an official of the country's the main sunflower seed processor, Cereol Rt said on Tuesday.
"Fungal diseases seem to be a specific feature of the Carpathian basin," Cereol Deputy General Director Ferenc Toth told Reuters.
He added that he expected a total sunflower seed harvest of between 700,000 and 750,000 tonnes.
According to Central Statistical Office figures, last year's sunflower seed crop was 868,000 tonnes and the 1995 harvest was 789,000 tonnes.
The Ministry for Agriculture, however, had higher expectations than Cereol, with ministry official Zsolt Kiraly estimating a crop of between 850,000 and 900,000 tonnes.
Toth explained the difference by the fact that the ministry's estimate was based on earlier information.
"Fungal disease and weed are present in many lots...and I wish the ministry's estimates were correct," Toth said.
He said that of the total crop, some 650,000 to 680,000 tonnes would be suitable for industrial use and added that Cereol planned to purchase at least 500,000 tonnes of it.
"This is our minimal target, but 600,000 tonnes would be even better," he said, adding that Cereol's total pressing capacity was 720,000 tonnes of sunflower seed per year.
He also said that Cereol only exports oil and its main markets are the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia and Russia.
Cereol is a member of the Eridania Beghin-Say agricultural group and controls 98 percent of Hungary's sunflower oil processing.
On the Budapest Commodity Exchange, sunflower seed futures settled on Monday at 44,250 forints per tonne for September and 44,000 forints for December.
